surface: COMMUNITY ROOM / Resident to Hyvor sign-in

readerContract.humanQuestion: How do I join this room with my LAiDIES account and return safely?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Sign in once, choose a public display name if needed, and return to the selected conversation.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: The visitor is on a community room and may have a Resident account.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: LAiDIES authenticates the Resident account; Hyvor hosts public comments and moderation.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A person can sign in, name themselves for a public room, and know whether the conversation actually opened.
readerContract.surfaceJob: Make the existing one-account community handoff understandable, truthful and recoverable.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I know what I am signing into, where I will return, and what did or did not happen.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any edit to a displayed sign-in, provider, return or error state.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Use the LAiDIES account to enter the selected conversation; choose a public display name only when the room needs one.
causalSequence: A room asks the visitor to sign in with LAiDIES.
The Resident account returns to the selected room and may request a public display name.
Hyvor is checked before the UI says the public conversation is open.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A signed-out reader in Ask the Room follows the account link and returns to that room.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A reader reaches Mix CD Exchange and uses the same account handoff while retaining that room destination.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Use Sign in with LAiDIES, then return to the selected room and only comment after confirmation.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Status, one action, optional display-name form, provider confirmation and explicit recovery states.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Do not turn account status into a lesson, slogan, generic celebration or unverified posting claim.

humourPlan.noneReason: Direct status language is safer for account and public-comment states.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Use concrete status, consequence and next action rather than a lesson.

humanQuestion.reason: A visitor needs one sign-in that returns them to the selected conversation.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: The sign-in action and exact return state are listed.

usefulCuriosity.reason: This is an account handoff, not an explanatory hook.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: The states make the route, display-name choice and provider confirmation visible.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: Checking, return, display-name, confirmation and error states are extracted.

limitationsConsequences.reason: Public comments and provider limits must remain explicit.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: Public-comment and provider failure text are extracted.

humourSurprise.reason: No humour is required in sign-in recovery.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The useful next action is joining the selected room.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: Return target and sign-in button are bound.

explanationArc.adaptation: The interactive needs truthful state transitions, not a substantial explanation.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The interface may imply a private Card signs a public comment, or claim a conversation opened before Hyvor accepts it.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Exercise signed out, account return, display name, provider success, provider failure and logout against the exact text artifact.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can distinguish account sign-in, public display name, provider confirmation and recoverable failure.
